evals.prompt: Write scripts/compress-logs.sh: given a directory argument, find every .log file under it (recursively), compress each one with gzip, and trap errors so temporary files are cleaned up on failure. Status messages go to stderr; print a JSON summary of compressed files to stdout. Run it against logs/ to show it works.
evals.expected_output: The script begins with a #!/bin/bash shebang and uses set -e for fail-fast error behavior.
expectations: scripts/compress-logs.sh starts with a bash shebang and enables fail-fast behavior (set -e or set -euo pipefail)
A trap cleans up temporary files on error or exit
Only .log files are compressed, recursively, and logs/notes.txt is left untouched
Status output goes to stderr and the JSON summary goes to stdout
The script is run against logs/ and the result is shown
